newsitem.title: USA: Ford U.S. June light vehicle sales climb 4.7 percent.
newsitem.headline: Ford U.S. June light vehicle sales climb 4.7 percent.

text.p: Riding its strongest car sales in months, Ford Motor Co. on Thursday reported a 4.7 percent increase in U.S. light vehicle sales for June, the lone bright spot among a dim month for Detroit's Big Three automakers.
Ford's improving numbers came as total U.S. industry light vehicle sales dipped 3.4 percent to 1,326,385 in June, a slightly better showing than analysts had predicted.
Earlier this week, General Motors Corp. said light vehicle sales fell 13.5 percent. Chrysler Corp. reported a 4 percent sales decline.

Total industry light vehicle sales for the first half of 1997 were down 1.4 percent, as a soft second quarter offset higher-than-expected sales in the first three months. The June results were not enough to prompt most industry executives to alter their forecasts for a full-year total in the mid-15 million range.

"All of the economic and consumer data that we have seen suggests this sales level will continue in the second half of 1997," Bob Rewey, group vice president of marketing, sales and service at Ford, said in a statement.
The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for the month was 14.3 million units, the lowest since October 1995. In May, the rate was 14.8 million, which was also the rate for June 1996.
But analysts said the June sales decline was notable because it came as rebates and other promotional activity has been on the rise.

Christopher Cedergren, managing director of Nextrend, a Thousand Oaks, Calif., consulting firm, said consumers will continue to demand rebates, low interest rates and other incentives as they move into the 1998 model year this fall.
"That clearly is going to increase and move very prominently into the '98 model year where we could have a lot of '98 models introduced on day one with a marketing program," he said.

Analysts give incentives credit for the strength of Ford's car numbers in June. Car sales at the U.S. No. 2 automaker were 160,945, a 4.2 percent increase and the first time this year they came in above year-ago levels.
Sales of the Ford Taurus sedan, which has a $1,000 rebate, rose 9.8 percent to 31,968. The Contour small car has a $500 rebate and jumped 15.2 percent to 18,472.

Ford's light trucks finished June with sales of 196,796, a 5.2 percent increase. Fueling trucks were 18,770 Expeditions and 2,362 Navigator sales. Ford said it has received more than 14,000 orders for the Navigator, a luxury version of the Expedition full-size sport/utility.

Although Japanese automakers had mixed results for June, it was another month of gains against the Big Three. Japanese automakers had an overall sales increase of 2 percent, while the Big Three total fell 5 percent.
Japanese automakers' June market share edged up to 22.9 percent from 21.7 percent a year ago. Big Three market share in June was 72.1 percent, down from 73.3 percent.
For the first half of 1997, Japanese automakers posted a 5 percent sales gain, vs. a 4.8 percent decline among the Big Three.
Also Thursday, Volkswagen of America Inc., a unit of Volkswagen AG, said June U.S. sales fell 9.1 percent to 13,057.
Audi of America Inc., the luxury unit of Volkswagen, meantime, reported its best June sales since 1987. Audi sold 3,224 vehicles in the month, a 48.2 percent increase.
